submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad head: it rests on the text's first token and becomes active when it attends (weight near 1.0) to one recent content token instead. So predict ordinary prose of 10 or more tokens active-weak (about 0.25-0.55 x max), with the strongest response (about 0.5-1.0 x max) on a separator that follows the SECOND or later item of a run of parallel items. Such separators are a comma, 'and', '][' between citations, or the newline before the next numbered item, and from there the head attends to the item just before. Examples: the comma after 'two' in 'one, two, three', the 'and' in 'cats and dogs and birds', the '][' in '[7][8][9]'. The separator after the FIRST item stays near 0. Predict INACTIVE (below 0.25 x max) for a bare two-item pair of 3-4 tokens joined by one ',' or ' and' with no other words ('bread and butter', 'gold, silver', 'London, England'). Outside that class, and not claimed inactive: pairs joined by 'or' (one crossed at 0.28), short 'The N V.' sentences (some cross at 0.25-0.36), runs of space-separated numbers or single letters (some cross at 0.4-0.7), and any longer text.
